verdict.rationale: Ironclad documents contract creation in a no-code builder and a controlled workflow layer. That layer includes Workflow Designer, launchable workflows, and platform-enforced approval and signature policies. The docs also mention updating contract language and uploading new document versions. However, negotiation and redlining, such as tracked changes or counterparty markup, are only implied and never explicitly documented. missing for 10: explicit redlining/tracked-changes capability, documented counterparty negotiation features, independent hands-on corroboration of the negotiation flow.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, I can draft, negotiate, and redline contracts in a controlled workflow instead of email attachments

citations.quote: leaving the specifics around updating contract language and following approval and signature policies to the Ironclad platform
integrations can interface directly with underlying contract documents, reading contract text or updating new versions of the document
The corresponding Workflows API allows you to retrieve, create, and interact with active and completed workflows.
